artifacts.title: Plain-text workaround search
artifacts.scope: Bounded search for portable text use and image, prose, custom-font, or PUA workarounds.
limitations: Family-level workaround classes do not establish three qualifying examples for any individual record.

artifacts.title: 1980s and 1990s historical visual-gap report
artifacts.scope: Sampled primary manufacturer manuals for historical response-curve and standalone-glyph evidence.
limitations: The bounded sample cannot establish a complete industry lineage or prove absence outside the reviewed manuals.

artifacts.title: Current representation matrix
artifacts.scope: Compared terminology and representation treatments in eight current vendor sources.
limitations: The source set is not a market census, and mutable online documentation may change.

artifacts.title: Band-stop and notch semantic boundary report
artifacts.scope: Tested exact-alias, narrow-subtype, response-region, and product-mode uses of notch and band-stop.
limitations: No reviewed standards-body source supplied a universal numerical boundary.

artifacts.title: Unicode and adjacent-standards overlap audit
artifacts.scope: Reproducibly audited Unicode 17 semantic candidates, visual near-misses, sequences, and IEC 60617 terminology for all four records.
limitations: Later Unicode versions, restricted IEC data sheets, IEC 60417, ISO 7000, and font-by-font rendering were outside scope.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Synthesized project evidence and counterevidence merged through PR 24 without changing record state.
limitations: A synthesis is not an independent source and cannot increase source-independence counts.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Superseding six-record status synthesis for registry 0.2.0, including conservative shelf-record assessments and unresolved gates.
limitations: A synthesis is not an independent source and cannot increase source-independence counts.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Superseding six-record status synthesis for registry 0.2.1 after the bounded shelf overlap audit, without reassessment or status movement.
limitations: The recorded shelf scores predate DA-009; this synthesis does not infer score movement from completing the audit.

artifacts.title: Shelf history, education, trade-media, and community report
artifacts.scope: Compared historical manuals and teaching material, current education, trade media, and practitioner discussion for shelf semantics, representation, text friction, and boost/cut polarity.
limitations: The bounded English-language sample is not an industry census and does not prove absence of portable shelf-glyph use elsewhere.

artifacts.title: Low-shelf and high-shelf vendor semantics
artifacts.scope: Tested whether low-shelf and high-shelf side semantics remain stable across gain sign and compared compact selectors, contextual curves, and text or hardware controls.
limitations: The purposive sample is not a market census and did not inspect running product builds or establish a shared standalone contour.

artifacts.title: Low-shelf and high-shelf Unicode and standards overlap audit
artifacts.scope: Reproducibly audited Unicode 17 semantic candidates, shelf lexical collisions, smooth-fork visual near-misses, text sequences, and ISO/IEC 10646, SMuFL, IEC, and AES adjacency for the provisional shelf pair.
limitations: Restricted standards content, exhaustive IEC 60417 and ISO 7000 entry search, subscriber-only AES material, font-by-font rendering, and participant recognition were outside scope.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Superseding six-record status synthesis for registry 0.2.2 after the bounded shelf overlap audit and shelf text-friction search, without reassessment or status movement.
limitations: The recorded shelf scores predate DA-009 and DA-010; this synthesis does not infer score movement from completing either analysis.

artifacts.title: Low-shelf and high-shelf plain-text-friction search
artifacts.scope: Bounded per-record search for low-shelf and high-shelf ambiguous, lossy, image-dependent, or other workaround-dependent text communication.
limitations: The English-language sample is not a census; this search does not clear the per-record numerical safeguard, and clearing it in future would not itself establish portable-glyph practice or Unicode readiness.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Post-evidence six-record status synthesis after mechanical shelf overlap reassessment, without semantic or status movement.
limitations: The shelf plain-text-friction safeguard remains open, and the reassessment does not establish recognition, artwork acceptance, external support, or Unicode readiness.

artifacts.title: Four-record target-use evidence spike
artifacts.scope: Bounded audit and primary-source reinspection for target-use and visual-convergence gaps in the four original filter-response records.
limitations: The two-source spike is not a market census, imports no third-party artwork, excludes Notch from band-stop unless a source explicitly binds the broader concept, and changes no semantics, aliases, artwork, status, or external position.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Six-record status synthesis after the four-record target-use evidence spike and mechanical reassessment, without semantic, alias, artwork, or status movement.
limitations: Band-pass lifecycle remains unchanged despite numerical eligibility; high-pass and low-pass retain material alias blockers, band-stop retains the Notch and fallback blockers, and all formal Unicode safeguards remain in force.

artifacts.title: Unicode proposal critical-path audit
artifacts.scope: Mapped the current authoritative non-emoji Unicode proposal requirements and every remaining six-concept readiness gap while preserving formal proposal HOLD.
limitations: The bounded pipeline and non-approval searches do not cover every UTC or WG2 document or alternate term; no legal conclusion is offered about evidence figures, font licensing, CLAs, or AI-assisted authorship.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Superseding six-record status synthesis after the four-record target-use evidence spike, mechanical reassessment, and Unicode proposal critical-path audit, without semantic, alias, artwork, or status movement.
limitations: Band-pass lifecycle remains unchanged despite numerical eligibility; high-pass and low-pass retain material alias blockers, band-stop retains the Notch and fallback blockers, and all formal Unicode safeguards remain in force.
The Unicode HOLD remains active; current guidance evidence does not establish independent character use, community-level form stability, or public plain-text interchange need.

artifacts.title: Independent character-like use and plain-text need spike
artifacts.scope: Bounded public search for independent character-like implementations, portable plain-text interchange, and image, prose, ASCII, PUA, custom-font, or icon-package workarounds across the six active filter-response concepts.
limitations: The search is not a market census; mutable or authentication-gated results were excluded where they could not be reproduced, derivative icon packaging is not counted as independent adoption, and no portable character use was found.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Superseding six-record status synthesis after the independent character-like use and plain-text need spike, preserving the Unicode guidance audit and making no assessment, semantic, alias, artwork, or status movement.
limitations: No portable independent text use was recovered; icon-font implementation and image/prose friction do not establish encoding necessity, and all formal Unicode safeguards remain in force.

artifacts.title: Band-stop render and alias evidence spike
artifacts.scope: Bounded search for a second direct axis-less band-stop or band-reject implementation and independent provenance for the existing BSF and band reject terms, with Notch-only evidence excluded.
limitations: Two implementations are not a market census or artwork license; engineering abbreviation support does not establish common audio-professional plain-text use; the band-stop/Notch boundary remains unresolved.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Superseding six-record status synthesis after the band-stop render and terminology evidence spike, preserving the prior complete synthesis by reference and making no assessment, semantic, alias, artwork, or status movement.
limitations: The second-render and terminology-provenance gaps are evidence-complete only for mechanical reassessment; the band-stop/Notch boundary, common audio plain-text usage, recognition, artwork rights, and lifecycle requirements remain open.

artifacts.title: Six-concept communication-failure casebook
artifacts.scope: Bounded independent public casebook of image attachment, labeling requests, undocumented symbols, cross-product lookup, and documentation mislabeling across the six active filter-response concepts.
limitations: The search is not a prevalence estimate, low shelf alone meets the casebook's conservative recurrence threshold, no hand-drawn compact glyph used as a plain-text substitute or failed text-only exchange was recovered, and no case establishes portable character use or Unicode eligibility.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Superseding six-record status synthesis after the communication-failure casebook, preserving the prior complete synthesis by reference and making no assessment, semantic, alias, artwork, or status movement.
limitations: The low-shelf recurrence result is bounded communication-friction evidence, not a prevalence estimate, portable character use finding, encoding necessity claim, or Unicode eligibility determination; all formal safeguards remain in force.

artifacts.title: Six-concept repertoire stability and semantic-boundary dossier
artifacts.scope: Decade-spanning, cross-lane assessment of semantic stability, terminology boundaries, representation variation, and coherence for the authorized six-concept audio-filter repertoire.
limitations: The purposive English-language corpus is not market-weighted, and stable software or engineering taxonomies do not establish stable standalone character forms, portable glyph use, or Unicode eligibility.
No universal drawing identity, exact notch/band-stop threshold, unrestricted pass/cut alias policy, participant recognition result, or external standards position is asserted.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Superseding six-record status synthesis after the repertoire-stability dossier, preserving the merged independent-use, band-stop, and communication casebook evidence without semantic, alias, artwork, assessment, or status movement.
limitations: The low-shelf recurrence result is bounded communication-friction evidence, not a prevalence estimate, portable character use finding, encoding necessity claim, or Unicode eligibility determination; all formal safeguards remain in force.
DA-017 supports the coherence of the six semantic classes but does not establish universal glyph forms, independent character use, or Unicode eligibility.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Superseding six-record status synthesis after mechanical reassessment of EV-120 through EV-151 and the independently reviewed D-021 band-pass registry-candidate transition.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis

artifacts.title: Band-stop and Notch adverse boundary dossier
artifacts.scope: Adverse comparison of Band-stop and Notch definitions, labels, Q and width treatment, direct implementations, and education or user practice, bounded to the current semantic blocker and 15/20 gaps.
limitations: The purposive English-language sample is not market-weighted and establishes no universal numeric Q or width boundary.
Notch-only evidence remains excluded unless its source explicitly maps or contrasts it with the broad Band-stop class; unrelated glyph and usage claims never transfer.
The dossier recommends a later reassessment but makes no semantic, alias, artwork, assessment, status, study, Unicode, release, or outreach change.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Superseding six-record status synthesis after the adverse Band-stop/Notch boundary dossier, preserving private font-proof validation without semantic, alias, artwork, assessment, or status movement.
limitations: DA-020 recommends a later mechanical reassessment but does not itself change the immutable assessment snapshot, eligibility, or lifecycle status.
Text/accessibility and visual-convergence gaps remain open; Notch-only implementations, glyphs, and usage remain excluded without explicit source-local mapping or contrast.
The private font proof and the dossier establish neither independent character use nor Unicode eligibility; Unicode remains HOLD.

artifacts.title: Pass/cut alias-equivalence dossier
artifacts.scope: Adverse cross-lane assessment of Low Cut as a high-pass alias and High Cut as a low-pass alias, separating response-class retrieval from implementation and arbitrary-phrase equivalence.
limitations: The purposive English-language corpus is not market-weighted, and publisher repetition is collapsed rather than treated as independent support.
The finding supports bounded audio-domain alias lookup, not equality of filter order, slope, Q, resonance, phase, cutoff convention, parameters, presets, or every product feature bearing a cut label.
This analysis changes no live semantic record; its recommendation requires separate D-021 semantic review.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis

limitations: The bounded alias recommendation does not itself change a live record and does not establish implementation equivalence, portable character use, encoding necessity, or Unicode eligibility.
The Band-stop controlled-polysemy recommendation remains pending its separate reassessment, and Notch-only evidence remains excluded under DA-020.
The private font proof and all three dossiers establish neither independent character use nor Unicode eligibility; Unicode remains HOLD.

artifacts.title: Shelf fork form-stability spike
artifacts.scope: Tests whether the locked shelf pair's axis-free, sign-agnostic, affected-side two-prong topology is independently established across current, historical, open-source, and educational sources without altering or importing artwork.
limitations: The positive result establishes topology and orientation, not identical contour, isolated recognition, portable text use, artwork reuse rights, or Unicode eligibility.
Product-local UI context may contribute to recognition, and polarity-specific counterexamples prevent a universal-form claim.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
